18-02-opti-1: Night on the prairie. Grass as far as you can see.
18-02-opti-2: The sun rises. Every blade gets bright, full light.
18-02-opti-3: Out here, wind blows, and rain comes and goes.
18-02-opti-4: Now a forest. Drop from the treetops…
18-02-opti-5: …down, as the leaves block the sun.
18-02-opti-6: On the forest floor, it's dim, cool, and damp.
18-02-opti-7: A fern? Down here, where the sun barely reaches?
18-02-opti-8: Its fronds spread wide and flat. Why that shape?
18-02-opti-9: Two homes, two very different plants. Why?
18-02-opti-10: Let's compare plants from two different places.
18-02-warm: Two new places today: a sunny prairie and a shady forest. Look closely at our first plant before we explain anything.
18-02-lesson: Today you compare. Watch a prairie come back after a fire, test leaves in the wind, and drop from the treetops to the dim forest floor.
18-02-check: Three quick questions. It's not graded. It's just for you, so give each one your best try.
18-02-assign: Your turn to compare. Name a trait, name its home, then say what problem it solves there.
18-02-words: Adaptation. Trait. Advantage. Environment. Survive. Variation.
how-18-02-compare: Drag the wide sheet under one tray and the thin strip under the other, or tap each one, then tap a tray. Press Turn on the wind. Then swap them and press it again.
how-18-02-partc: Draw your forest plant and grassland plant side by side. Under each one, write its biggest survival advantage.
